_comment: Rename to tracked_movies.json to activate. Titles or slugs both work and format suffixes are not needed: 'Lenin' matches 'Lenin (2D - Telugu)' and 'Lenin (IMAX - Telugu)'.
_mode: 'all' collects every movie (same as having no file). 'selected' collects ONLY the list below.
_store_all: true = disable the destructive scrape-time filter entirely; EVERY movie at every venue is scraped and stored (raw files, R2, combined data), regardless of 'mode'/'movies' above. The dashboard build (build_data.py) still applies 'mode'/'movies' independently, so the SITE only shows the listed titles while the raw data keeps everything (e.g. for full per-venue/multiplex analysis). Default false = old destructive behaviour (scrape only stores the tracked list).
_hide_untracked: Applies to movies ALREADY collected. true (default) = the dashboard shows only the tracked list, everything else vanishes from the site. false = already-collected movies stay visible and the list only limits NEW scraping. Either way the raw data in R2 is untouched, so this is reversible.
_dubs: A film released under a DIFFERENT TITLE per language is a SEPARATE movie with its own card. List each title you want tracked. Example: Jana Nayagan (Tamil), Jana Nayakudu (Telugu), Jan Neta (Hindi) are three entries, not one.
_warning: With store_all=false (default), filtering happens during the SCRAPE, so untracked movies are never stored going forward - adding a title later gives it NO back-history. With store_all=true, everything is always stored regardless of when a title is added to the list; only the dashboard display is affected.
_release_dates: REAL release date (YYYY-MM-DD) per film. Release day = Day 1; every date BEFORE it shows as Premiere on the dashboard and in Historical. REQUIRED for any film that has premiere / paid-preview shows, because then the earliest date with bookings is NOT the release date. Titles or slugs both work.
